name: Sharwa
sweep_summary: Sharwa (shar1249) is not in the catalog and Glottolog lists no grammar or phonology for it (5 refs: two wordlists/surveys by Brye 2003/2009, two Barreteau et al. overviews, and Gravina 2012). The single title-sweep item, Gravina 2012 'Vowels, consonants and prosody in two Central Chadic languages' (WOCAL 6 proceedings, Köppe, pp. 7-20; hhtype minimal), is print-only with no DOI and no open copy anywhere reachable; its 'prosody' is almost certainly the Chadic consonant/vowel palatalization-labialization prosody of Jimi and Sharwa that Gravina's 2014 thesis (same author, same two languages, sec. 6.2) develops while explicitly excluding tone and stress. The Brye 2009 wordlist (on file) shows tone marks only. No first-hand Sharwa word-stress statement was read; best_new_statement not found. Priority for acquiring Gravina 2012 is medium: it is the only phonological description of Sharwa in print, so worth a library check, but the author's own framing makes a stress statement unlikely. Everything fetched sources is under with.

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard (2012). Vowels, consonants and prosody in two Central Chadic languages. In Matthias Brenzinger & Anne-Maria Fehn (eds.), Proceedings of the 6th World Congress of African Linguistics, Cologne 2009, 7-20. Cologne: Rüdiger Köppe. (Glottolog ref 549116; hhtype 'minimal'; languages Jimi [jim] + Sharwa [swq])
